text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Foreign Minister Levy: Reliable intelligence information shows Arabs have decided to isolate us.
- Prime Minister Netanyahu to propose at Lisbon conference regional cooperation mechanism.
MAARIV
- Netanyahu approves 350 housing units in Jordan Valley.
- Treasury to propose defence cuts despite opposition from Netanyahu.
HAARETZ
- Netanyahu, in Lisbon, will blame Arafat for delaying negotiations.
- Parliament's Finance Committee intends to recommend that the Treasury raise VAT and cigarette tax.
- Mandate of U.N. observer force on the Golan Heights is extended for another six months.
GLOBES
- Securities Authority rejects Leumi Insurance Holdings prospectus, awaits explanations.
- After straight rises since June, $4.4 million drop in foreign currency reserves for November.
- 30 percent drop in November building starts on Housing Ministry, Land Administration land.
- Finance Minister Meridor: Government will not increase tax burden if spending cut substantially.
JERUSALEM POST
- Prime minister rejects Arab verbal attacks.
- Prime minister to approve more housing for Jordan Valley settlements.
- Jewish Agency works to free doomed Grozny Jew facing execution.
- Israel and Turkey agree to continue defence accord.
- Syria's chemical arms to head agenda at U.S.-Israel talks.
